    Polynomial kernels of pencils on arbitrary vector spaces #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.polynomial_pencil_injective {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module k V] [Module k W] (A B : V →ₗ[k] W) (h : Function.Injective ⇑(A + B)) :
    Function.Injective ⇑(LinearMap.baseChange (Polynomial k) A + Polynomial.X • LinearMap.baseChange (Polynomial k) B)

    If a pencil is injective at one, it has no nonzero polynomial kernel vectors. The source and target may have arbitrary dimension.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.eq_zero_of_pencil_intertwiner {k : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3} [Field k] [AddCommGroup V] [AddCommGroup W] [Module k V] [Module k W] {E : Type u_4} {F : Type u_5} [AddCommGroup E] [AddCommGroup F] [Module k E] [Module k F] [Module.Finite k E] [Module.Finite k F] (d t : E →ₗ[k] F) (hd : Function.Surjective ⇑d) (v : E) (hv : d v = 0) (A B : V →ₗ[k] W) (hi : Function.Injective ⇑(A + B)) (m : E →ₗ[k] V) (n : F →ₗ[k] W) (hA : A ∘ₗ m = n ∘ₗ d) (hB : B ∘ₗ m = n ∘ₗ t) :
    m v = 0

    Transport a null vector of a finite-dimensional surjective pencil at zero to another pencil. If the second pencil is injective at one, the transported vector at zero vanishes, even when its space is infinite-dimensional.
